To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gut barrier function and gut microbiota are altered in food deprivation, food restrictions and protein energy wasting, and that these changes are related to each other.
food restriction, protein energy wasting, and food deprivation induce changes in gut barrier structure and function, and gut microbiota composition.

1) food restriction and protein malnutrition are associated with an increased gut permeability and a decreased gut barrier integrity, 2) food restriction and starvation lead to a decreased gut immune function, and 3) food restriction is associated with a changed gut microbiota composition and a changed gut microbiome function
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the gut barrier in the regulation of energy metabolism and body weight.
the impact of food intake and nutritional state on the gut barrier and the gut microbiota, and the role of the latter on energy metabolism, and vice versa.
the gut microbiota in relation to gut barrier function and the enteric neuroendocrine system in food restriction, protein energy wasting and food deprivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gut barrier function is impaired in depleted states.
gut microbiota, gut barrier and gut nervous system interact and are altered in depleted nutritional states.
gut microbiota and intestinal barrier are affected by food restriction, food depletion and protein energy wasting, which in turn influence the nutritional status and the immune function of the host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
food restriction and protein-energy wasting, but also food deprivation, alter gut barrier function and gut microbiota, and that these two compartments are in a close relationship.
gut barrier is altered in depleted nutritional states, which is associated with gut microbiota alterations.
food deprivation and food restriction, and more specifically protein energy wasting, induce changes of the gut microbiota composition and function that in turn influence gut barrier function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gut microbiota and its metabolites may be a promising tool for the prevention and treatment of depleted states.
gut barrier is not only a physical barrier, but also a dynamic and interactive structure, which is involved in the regulation of energy metabolism and nutrient sensing.
the gut microbiota is an important factor in determining gut barrier function, and that the latter is a key factor in determining the nutritional state of the host.
